title: It’s Hard To Predict Who Will Be Suicidal. It’s Easier To Ensure People Can’t Shoot Themselves.
summary: Some mental health experts favor suicide prevention steps that are applied broadly, with protections that aren’t tied to an individual’s specific risk.

title: Health Journalists Visit Conservative Georgia District and Weigh AI Bioweapon Threat
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: Cost-Saving Medicaid Meal Deliveries Threatened by Cuts, Policy Uncertainty
summary: An experiment to provide meals to some Medicaid recipients shows food can be cost-effective medicine. But even as federal officials tout the power of nutrition, Medicaid budget cuts could lead states to think twice about covering healthy food for sick residents. One has already reconsidered.

title: The Drugs and Devices Have Been on the Market for Years. But FDA-Ordered Studies Still Aren’t Done.
summary: To get drugs and devices out faster, the FDA lets companies conduct studies of safety or efficacy after the products are approved. In many cases, such “postmarket” studies are behind schedule or overdue, records show.

title: Sticker Shock at the Doctor’s Office Could Motivate Midterm Voters
summary: Steep jumps in health insurance premiums and deductibles are top of mind for many voters heading into midterm elections. KFF Health News chief Washington correspondent Julie Rovner explains how rising costs may shape competitive races. She also distills plans from candidates on both sides of the aisle to bring costs down.

title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: California Eyes Prison Heat Protections That Fall Short of Workplace Standards
summary: California is crafting weaker heat protections for prisons than other workplaces, citing billions in costs to cool aging institutions as climate and health risks increase. It’s a second-class standard, health and safety advocates say, and would leave correctional workers more susceptible to heat illness.

title: 3 Common Drugs Older Adults Might Be Overusing
summary: Not all older people need benzodiazepines, antibiotics, or daily aspirin — and taking them can carry increased risks.

title: Outcome of Suit Against Department of Labor Could Boost Skimpy Employer Health Plans
summary: The case was brought by a marketing company that wants to define as employees people who download an app and agree to have their internet activity tracked so they can buy into its employee health plan. Such plans are generally exempt from some state and Affordable Care Act rules.

title: States Bet Big on Rural Health Startups, With a Silicon Valley Twist
summary: States are spending rural health dollars on tech startups, betting that untested companies will succeed where doctors have vanished and hospitals have collapsed. Louisiana’s call for innovative technology drew more than 200 pitches, seeking from $250,000 to $3 million in seed money.
